points.description: Correctly contrasts the two modes: asynchronous sends each character as an independent unit framed by a start bit and a stop bit (simple/cheap, low transmission rate), whereas synchronous sends many characters pooled together as a continuous stream/frame delimited by SYN/flag, needing sender-receiver synchronization (more complex, higher transmission rate). Equivalent wording accepted.
points.partial_credit: Award half if only one mode is described correctly, or the modes are described without the contrast (e.g., start/stop bits per character vs. blocks/frames).
